body: SLICE 7 IS YOURS - bd-01M16JQHDE89QJWT9MZ56G6HG3, P1, and it is the sharpest work left in the sweep. Three phantom-typed witnesses my own slice plan orphaned: AmrGraph[C <: CheckState, R <: RoleForm] (amr-interop/AmrGraph.scala:16), PropositionChart[C <: CheckState] (proposition/chart.scala:252), StoryModel[S <: ModelStatus] (story/model.scala:18). WHY THEY ARE WORSE THAN EVERY OTHER SITE: for a phantom-typed class the Mirror can be summoned AT ANY TYPE ARGUMENT, so Mirror.ProductOf[AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles]] resolves as readily as the unchecked one - the forger does not merely bypass validation, THE FORGER CHOOSES WHICH VALIDATION STATE TO CLAIM. Every other site lets you build an invalid value; these let you build a value that ASSERTS IT IS VALID. AmrGraph's Scaladoc promises 'downstream code can demand AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles] and be GUARANTEED that dangling references, missing concepts, and inverse spellings are gone' and 'checked graphs ONLY from AmrValidator'. PropositionChart[Checked] is already load-bearing in document/mention.scala TODAY. And this is design-contract rule 8 itself - 'invalid states are unrepresentable when rules are stable (Checked/Unchecked, Draft/Validated)' - which I amended twice tonight for the case-class half and never checked the phantom half of. REQUIRED: demonstrate the forge AT A CHECKED TYPE ARGUMENT specifically. The point is not that a graph can be built, it is that a graph asserting it was validated can be built without validation. Read docs/design/unforgeable-types.md first - criterion, three doors, and what does NOT close the door (a user-written companion does not suppress the Mirror). Your route candidate d821fee is under my gate now; five identities verified present, ProviderAbstained and AllMissing both used, no Ineligible for external-only as ruled.
